_README: Which trails each organization may put a challenge on (#1780, design principle 5:
'a challenge can only use places on trails its organization publishes').
A REVIEWED JUDGEMENT, NOT A DERIVATION, and it is its own file on purpose. The
pipeline has no single map from an organization to the trail ids its published
POIs carry: sources.json keys organizations as 'org:atc', a POI names its layer
as 'atc_viewpoints' (which sources.json does not list), and trail_emblems.json
spells trails as 'at' and 'long-path' where POIs say 'AT' and 'LP'. Letting a
challenge declare its own trail would make the scope rule circular, so the
scope lives here, one row per organization, with the reason it is true.
export_challenges.py checks every row: the org must be an organization in
sources.json, and every trail id must be carried by at least one published POI
(a trail with nothing placed on it can hold no challenge place).

publishers.why: The ATC is the A.T.'s route owner (sources.json org:atc) and every A.T. POI layer that ships - shelters, vistas, parking, privies, campsites, communities - is the ATC's.
